question: Using the customary setting of the mathematics used for quantum mechanics, is it possible to prove the existence of Gödelßs god-like entities?

1.text:
The mathematics which is customarily used for quantum mechanics is the
ordinary mathematics of Hilbert space theory, i.e. ZFC classically
interpreted with complex linear algebra, measure theory etc.  In that
background the modal first order language used by Gödel can be
interpreted, and the derivation

$P(x)\to N P(x)$ , $P(x)\to E P(x)$ etc.

can be written down as a formal derivation in S5+P.  That is all that
is ever meant by the “formal validity’’ of the ontological argument.

What cannot be obtained is a theorem of the physical formalism.  The
existence claim of the Gödel argument

$\exists xG(x)$ , $G(x) \equiv P(x)\wedge\forall P\,[\,P(x)\to P(x)\,]$

is a formal consequence only of the purely metaphysical axioms

* *P* is positive,
* $P$ positive $\to$ $N P$ positive,
* $P$ positive $\to$ $E P$ positive,
* $P$ & $Q$ positive $\to$ $P\vee Q$ positive,
* $\lnot P$ positive $\to$ $P$ is not positive,

and of the modal principles of S5.  None of those axioms is a
consequence of the Hilbert-space axioms

$\mathcal H$ a complex separable Hilbert space, 
$A=A^{\dagger}$ on $\mathcal H$, $\rho\ge0$, $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$,
etc.

and none of them can be read off the lattice of closed subspaces
$\mathcal L(\mathcal H)$, which is orthomodular and not Boolean.
The ontological argument is therefore not a theorem of quantum
mechanics; it is a translation of a modal-metaphysical argument into
the set-theoretic metalanguage in which Hilbert spaces are defined.

In particular the unconditional existence of a maximally positive
being in the formal system is a consistency statement for the
theory of positive properties.  By Gödel II the consistency of the
background set theory in which quantum mechanics is formulated cannot
be proved inside that background theory.  Hence the existence of a
Gödelian “god-like’’ entity remains a conditional claim, i.e. a
claim about the truth of the ontological axioms, not a consequence
of the physical mathematics of quantum mechanics proper.  That is
the usual sense in which the proof is not a physical proof at all.

2.text:
In the background set theory in which Hilbert spaces, C*-algebras, spectral
measures etc. are defined the proof can of course be written down. The
ordinary mathematics of quantum mechanics is classical mathematics,
ZFC + a complete complex pre-Hilbert space. In that meta-theory S5
modal first order logic is definable and Gödel's axioms

* P positive → ¬P not positive,
* P positive and P → Q  ⇒ Q positive,
* Nec P positive → P positive,
* P positive → P possible,
etc.,

are ordinary sentences of modal predicate logic. Once the axioms about
positivity are accepted the S5 derivation

G := ∃x Gx ,    Gx := ∀P [ P(x) → P positive ]

Necessarily P positive → P is positive for any P,  the usual
ontological derivation goes through in classical logic and can be
carried out inside ZFC. In that formal sense the argument is a theorem
of the classical meta-theory in which the Hilbert space formalism lives.

It is not a theorem of quantum mechanics. The propositional calculus
that is the natural logic of the physical propositions of quantum
theory is not a Boolean algebra at all but the orthomodular lattice
L(H) of closed subspaces / projection operators of a Hilbert space H.
L(H) is orthocomplemented, non-distributive, and it validates neither
the classical law of excluded middle nor the distributivity that is
used in the usual first order rendering of “positive property’’. The
Gödel axioms are essentially Boolean/modal axioms about an abstract
universe of properties. They have no canonical interpretation as
projections, observables or states of a quantum system, and the
classical modal S5 consequence relation is not the consequence relation
of quantum logic.

So one can reproduce the formal S5 proof in the classical set theory
that underlies the mathematical formalism of QM, but the premises about
positivity are metaphysical, not physical, and they cease to be available
once the logical structure is restricted to the orthomodular propositional
structure which is the content of the quantum formalism. In particular
no new physical existence statement about states, observables or
systems follows from the Schrödinger / Heisenberg / von Neumann axioms.
The ontological argument remains a classical modal-logical claim about
an abstract property-sphere, not a consequence of the Hilbert-space
mathematics of quantum mechanics.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion concerns the formal status of Gödel’s ontological argument in the classical set-theoretic meta-theory in which quantum-mechanical mathematics lives, not in the physical propositional structure of QM itself.

Both colleagues agree on the core point:
* The customary mathematics for QM is classical: ZFC + complex separable Hilbert space, C*-algebras, spectral measures, etc. In that classical background modal first-order logic S5 and Gödel’s positivity axioms can be written as ordinary sentences, and the standard S5 derivation of ∃x Gx with Gx := P(x) ∧ ∀P [P(x)→ □P(x)] goes through formally once the metaphysical axioms about positivity are accepted.
* The axioms used are:
  – P positive → ¬P not positive,
  – closure under implication, Necessity, Possibility, disjunction, etc.,
  – the principle that positive properties imply necessary positivity.
  None of these is a consequence of Hilbert-space axioms H a complex Hilbert space, A=A†, ρ≥0, trρ=1, etc., nor of the lattice L(H) of closed subspaces/projections.

Colleague 1 emphasizes the modal-metaphysical character and Gödel II: the unconditional existence of a maximally positive being is a consistency claim for the theory of positive properties; consistency of the background set theory cannot be proved inside it, so the “existence’’ remains conditional on the ontological axioms, not a physical theorem.

Colleague 2 emphasizes the logical structure mismatch: the natural logic of physical propositions in QM is the orthomodular lattice L(H), non-distributive, non-Boolean, and does not validate the classical Boolean/modal reasoning used in the Gödel argument. Hence the positivity axioms have no canonical interpretation as projections, observables or states, and S5 consequence is not the consequence relation of quantum logic.

Thus the consensus so far is:
Formal provability: Yes in the classical ZFC meta-theory that underlies QM formalism.
Physical provability: No. The argument is not a theorem of the Schrödinger/Heisenberg/von Neumann axioms, and it does not yield a new existence statement about states, observables or systems. The proof is a classical modal-logical claim about an abstract property sphere, transferred into the set-theoretic language used to define Hilbert spaces.

Unresolved / to keep in mind: whether any non-trivial interpretation of “positive property’’ can be given inside the orthomodular propositional structure without collapsing to classical Boolean logic, and whether the claim “possible to prove” is to be read as formal derivability in the meta-theory vs. derivability from physical postulates. My current belief leans to the second reading: no physical proof, only a formalizable classical modal argument in the background set theory.

A separable complex Hilbert space, a self-adjoint operator, a density operator $\rho\ge 0$, $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, a spectral measure, a $C^{*}$-algebra, etc. are all defined in ZFC classically interpreted. $Gx \equiv P(x)\wedge\forall P\,[\,P(x)\to \Box P(x)\,]$,

* $P$ positive and $P\to Q$ $\to$ $Q$ positive,
* $P$ positive $\to \Box P$ positive,
* $P$ positive $\to \Diamond P$, etc.

are accepted it is a theorem of the classical meta-theory in which the Hilbert-space formalism lives.

The physical content of the formalism is the orthomodular lattice $\mathcal L(\mathcal H)$ of closed subspaces / projections, or equivalently the non-commutative $C^{*}$-algebra of observables and states. $\mathcal L(\mathcal H)$ is orthocomplemented, non-distributive and non-Boolean. The Boolean distributivity, excluded middle and the S5 modal consequence used in Gödel’s derivation are not the consequence relation of quantum logic, and the Gödel positivity axioms have no canonical interpretation as properties of projections, observables or states. None of the positivity closure conditions is a consequence of

$\mathcal H$ complex Hilbert, $A=A^{\dagger}$, $\rho\ge0$, $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$,

etc.

Hence $\exists x Gx$ is not derivable from the Schrödinger/Heisenberg/von Neumann axioms. What is obtained is a classical modal-metaphysical claim about an abstract property sphere, formalizable in the ZFC meta-theory that is used to define Hilbert spaces, but it yields no new existence statement about states, observables or physical systems. The existence of a Gödelian maximally positive being remains conditional on the unprovable ontological axioms, and by Gödel II the consistency of the background set theory cannot be proved inside it. In the physical sense the proof is simply not available from the mathematics of quantum mechanics proper.

$Gx\equiv P(x)\wedge\forall P\,[P(x)\to\Box P(x)]\;\equiv\;\forall P\,[P(x)\to P\;{\rm positive}]$

and the Gödel positivity axioms

* $P$ positive $\to\neg P$ not positive,
* $P$ positive and $P\to Q\Rightarrow Q$ positive,
* $P$ positive $\to\Box P$ positive, $P$ positive $\to\Diamond P$,

closure under $\vee,\wedge$ etc., the S5 derivation of $\exists x\,Gx$ is a purely syntactic theorem of the classical meta-theory in which $\mathcal H$ lives. – P positive → □P positive / Nec P positive, P positive → ◇P;
– etc.
